title: Python: restore the edges of calls in a class-body alias's PEP 696 default (recall, not a wrong edge; DEC-303 (a77) item 4)
description: Ordinary follow-up (recall, not a hold item), DEC-303 (a77) item 4. GCLI-146 (landed 18b68a7) refuses every call in a class-body alias's PEP 696 default (type A[T = x.run()] = int, type A[T = f()] = int), with or without a later class-body binding, by the SUPERSET rule: typeParameterNames counts every identifier under a parse error in a type-parameter list as a type-parameter name (this grammar parses a default as an ERROR node of the type parameter's name plus a sibling type node holding the call), so the call's names resolve to type parameters and refuse. origin/dev gave C.run and f there (measured), so dev's correct edges are lost; removal-only, accepted over-refusal, confined to class-body aliases, 3.13+ only. Restore them either by a grammar that parses PEP 696 defaults, or by counting only the binding positions under the error node as type-parameter names; any edge the restoration would create needs its own opum-doc ruling first. Fixtures pinning the over-refusal are in test/python-hops.test.ts (describe 'a class-body alias default refuses every call in it'); this task turns them into the restored edges. Not started.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Decide the restoration (a grammar that parses defaults, or only binding positions under the error node count) and report any edge it would create to opum-doc before building
The default fixtures (with and without a later import) updated to the restored edges, red before and green after, the subset check against dev and the 1394-source corpus, the five pins identical
